Subject: Follow-up: procurement next steps & vendor intake (Redwood)

Hi Aisha 

Great to meet you and Ben on the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the procurement side so your finance/procurement team has what they need to move forward: 

1) Paper process: We can support vendor setup via PO (net 30/45/60), corporate card, or the cloud marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure) depending on what's easiest for your procurement team.

2) Vendor packet: Attached is our standard vendor setup spreadsheet (vendor_setup_form.xlsx) that your team typically asks for  company details, tax classification, and banking remit. I also attached a stub of our W-9 for your records.

3) Marketplace: If you prefer marketplace procurement, we're listed on the AWS Marketplace  that can simplify billing but typically takes a separate procurement/legal sign-off. If that's an option, let me know and I'll put you in touch with our marketplace ops lead.

4) Timeline & owner: If you can share your preferred commercial path (PO vs card vs marketplace), I'll coordinate with our finance ops to kick off vendor onboarding. Marissa (cc'd) will own vendor intake from our side.

Next steps: 
- Can you confirm which path you want to pursue?
- I'll send the DocuSign link for the MSA if procurement requires it, or we can do a simple purchase order process if you're set.

Thanks  enjoyed the technical discussion as well.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Dylan 

Good recap. A few items from procurement before we can raise a PO: 
- We need a completed vendor setup form (we prefer XLSX) with bank routing for ACH payments, remit-to address, and tax classification.
- Our tax team will need a completed W-9 and a statement of whether Redwood is a US entity for withholding.
- Standard lead time for vendor setup is ~7-10 business days after we receive full packet; we prefer PO over card for enterprise spend.

Couple of clarifying Qs: 
1) Does Redwood require an upfront invoice or deposit for Dedicated capacity, or can we proceed with standard PO net-30?
2) If we go marketplace, does that change the invoicing cycle or available SKUs for Reserved/Dedicated capacity?

I've attached our internal vendor intake checklist so you can confirm required fields. Ben  I'm going to flag finance to expect the packet.

Hi Aisha 

Thanks for the details. To answer your questions quickly: 
- Upfront/deposit: For standard Hosted API usage we invoice net-30 on PO. For Dedicated/Reserved capacity we typically require an initial invoice upon provisioning for the first month (prorated) depending on the contract term; if finance prefers to use net terms we can structure the SOW so the first invoice aligns with net-30. I can share a short note from Finance Ops if you need explicit language for your procurement team.

- Marketplace: Purchasing through AWS Marketplace will change the billing flow (AWS bills you) and SKU availability can vary — Reserved capacity typically needs a separate marketplace listing. If you want to go marketplace, it usually adds 2-3 weeks to procurement onboarding but simplifies ongoing billing for some customers.

Attached: completed vendor_setup_form.xlsx (I filled in Redwood's company details and banking template), our W-9 (redwood_W-9.pdf), and the bank details template (bank_details_template.csv).

I've also included a DocuSign link to a standard MSA if your legal team prefers that route: https://redwood-inference.docusign.com/envelope/abc123

Marissa  can your team confirm the exact remit-to and bank fields so we match Orion's intake?

Next steps from our side:
- Please confirm PO vs card vs marketplace.
- If PO: Ben, if you can confirm a PO # and estimated spend band, we'll route this to Finance Ops and kick off vendor onboarding.

Thanks  happy to jump on a 15-min call if it helps speed the packet submission.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: vendor_setup_form.xlsx (completed stub), redwood_W-9.pdf (stub), bank_details_template.csv (stub)
